title: Precision of Longitudinal Proximal Treatment-Sequence Effects under Weakening Proxies
banked_reason: D0.5 math sound; promised all-band sharp frontier unresolved, incremental below field floor (score ceiling 5.2 < 7.4).
gap_reasons: The requested sharp all-band frontier is not delivered: the note proves a one-inverse lower bound only on g<=s/16, while its global estimator and interval attain only the two-inverse orders g^{-2} in root risk and length.
kernel_substituted@oeq:legal-orientation-phase: promised all-band sharp minimax-risk and honest-length frontier was replaced by an unresolved nonwedge phase question.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived an observed-law bridge formula, a positive parity/rescaling wedge lower experiment, and conservative finite-dimensional upper procedures. A scoped maximality retry examined the nonwedge legal orientations but produced only a definition of the unresolved stress program. The sharp all-band modulus and matching risk and interval rates remain open; the independent validity gate found no concrete bounded same-topic fix.
tldr: Repeated proxies identify treatment-sequence effects under evolving latent confounding, but fixed-law bridge formulas do not determine precision under triangular proxy weakening. In the positive absorbing two-occasion model, the proved contribution is a positive-law one-inverse all-procedure lower bound on \(0<g\le s/16\), together with observable global risk and measurable honest connected-interval upper guarantees at the two-inverse order. The sharp modulus on the remaining feasible region \(\mathcal D\cap\{g>s/16\}\) remains open: neither a uniform one-inverse upper bound nor a worse positive same-band lower construction is established. Accordingly, no globally sharp all-band frontier is claimed. The result is a bounded, coarsened benchmark for the three methotrexate sequences in Ying et al., conditional on the proximal model and coarsening checks.
gap: Longitudinal proximal theory provides identification, influence functions, and fixed-law efficiency, while recent weak-proxy work provides estimator-specific point-treatment bias bounds or broad impossibility results. None determines the all-procedure modulus, minimax risk, or honest connected-interval length for an absorbing treatment-sequence contrast over positive latent laws with linked first-stage and history strengths.
fill: The project first establishes the explicit wedge lower experiment and conservative global observable upper procedures. Its central solve target then derives the legal positive-law orientation geometry on every nonempty band, obtains the sharp modulus or corrected explicit phase surface, constructs positive within-band lower pairs for every phase, and transfers that surface to matching minimax and measurable honest connected-interval frontiers.
